What's the difference between Deuteran and Protan?
Deuteran is green type color blindness and Protan is red type color blindness, the article I got the image from explains it well.
Wow. The images are so similar! hard to imagine that a simple loss of Red or Green basically gets the same result.

You actually have less green photoreceptors, or they aren't as dominant when processing the signal.

One of the tricks compression algorithms use is they will take uncompressed files and only compress the green color space. You can compress the green rather heavily and not notice it, much much more than red or blue. Red/Blue contrast is sort of used as a second contrast pass of sorts, so compressing them is much more noticeable.

Also green receptors are unique in how they work as almost a boolean check for imaginary colors like fuscia. The way the mind processes color variance is cool, a photon packet at say 550 nanometers will trigger mild responses from green and red photoreceptors. So the brain sees mild responses from both and says "that must be yellow" and sort of "averages" the two signals together to get that color.

As you can see in OPs link, the EM spectrum we see is linear, its not a circle. Low wave lengths trigger blue, then green, then red, and our minds average the signals. But what happens when you mix blue and red? You get purple or fuscia and a whole set of hues in that range. But if you average the red and the blue you should land in the middle at green. But your brain says "no! there is no green receptors triggered! WTF!" and it fills in the gap by inventing a color between red and blue, turning the linear wave length chart into a color wheel.

I sometimes wonder if people who have Deuteran can see fuscia or if everything green triggers fuscia. But I would think their brains would notice the difference between little/no red/blue and BOTH red and blue. Still I bet there are people out there who see green as fuscia.
